request: How does successive halving decide which trials get more training?

composition.story: Start with equally trained trials and compare validation accuracy. Keep the stronger half, then resume only those trials with a larger budget. Advance through the checkpoints to see how each comparison determines who receives more training.

aha.observation: Successive halving gives more training only to the top half at each equal-budget checkpoint, using their current validation scores.

parts.presentation: Place below the explanation and above the experiment. Show the active checkpoint and completed trace here only. Steps represent states, not elapsed time. Reference captures show final-budget.

Use four fixed trial rows in alphabetical order. Align each named region with its readout. Highlight candidates participating in the current comparison or allocation. Keep stopped candidates visible; their frozen readouts preserve earlier evidence. No ghost or animation is needed.

Show cumulative training, validation accuracy, and allocation status beside each trial. Put the allocation entry below the rows as the bound status line. Assume fixed configurations, one validation set, equal epoch costs, and deterministic scores. Higher accuracy wins; alphabetical trial order breaks ties. Accuracy uses a shared percentage scale, rounded to whole percentage points. Epoch counts measure cumulative training from each trial's start. The initial checkpoint follows one epoch; later cumulative budgets double. Keep half the eligible trials at each selection. Survivors resume training rather than restart. Stopped trials never re-enter. All changing measurements come from the selected state's readouts.
Anchor beside the named trial without covering its readout. Identify the decision and explain its cause. Keep numeric evidence in the readouts only.

controls.label: Checkpoint
controls.presentation: Navigation budget: one index control. Parameter-control budget: none. Provide Previous and Next with accessible names, visible focus, and keyboard operation. Default to the first state; move one state per action. Bound navigation to the first and last states. Retain button names when disabled at boundaries. Every state, including final-budget, persists until learner action. No timer or autoplay.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Restore the first state and fixed defaults. Provide an accessible name, visible focus, and keyboard operation.

states.label: Keep the stronger survivor

states.why: The latest equal-budget comparison determines the next allocation, even though Trial A led earlier.

states.label: Allocation evidence

states.why: Repeated equal-budget comparisons concentrated training on survivors; eliminated trials received no further training.
